### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 805af4f290565955d6e6b56ee46fed45f721d955` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `29272acce0f217d79f3ba86df5b52af1c66c5fe7` — the merge of head `1c8c5ce75672323192ebaa9656e0aeed202ab9fe` into base `805af4f290565955d6e6b56ee46fed45f721d955`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 29272acce0f217d79f3ba86df5b52af1c66c5fe7 && git checkout 29272acce0f217d79f3ba86df5b52af1c66c5fe7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 805af4f290565955d6e6b56ee46fed45f721d955 1c8c5ce75672323192ebaa9656e0aeed202ab9fe && git checkout -B drift-repro 805af4f290565955d6e6b56ee46fed45f721d955 && git merge --no-ff 1c8c5ce75672323192ebaa9656e0aeed202ab9fe

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 805af4f290565955d6e6b56ee46fed45f721d955
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1c8c5ce75672323192ebaa9656e0aeed202ab9fe`

Scope: PR #20224 for card #20203 (`bug` · `priority:p2` · `domain:engine`). 7 files, +499/−9: `packages/core/src/utils/temporal-storage-form.ts` (+test), three new test files (driver-sql, driver-memory, rest), `.changeset/20203-epoch-ms-date-comparand.md` (added), `.changeset/20176-aggregation-temporal-storage-rule.md` (one line changed). Base = merge base with `origin/main` = `4df101c383`; the branch's merge of `main` at `16aedcab30` brought exactly one commit (`4df101c383`, #20213: `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/*`, `packages/spec/{api-surface,export-origins}/contracts.json`, one changeset) — intersection with the 7 PR files: empty; `git diff 4c8b92e022 16aedcab30 -- <7 files>`: empty. `packages/spec` untouched; no driver `src/` non-test file touched; no governed surface in the diff. `git merge-tree --write-tree` of head onto current `origin/main` (`805af4f290`) from a bare probe clone with no merge driver: clean (exit 0, tree `fe72a0b2b3`). Review owed by the `.changeset` prose face. Measured in detached worktrees at base and head under my scratch, closures built per tree; a real `InMemoryDriver` and a real `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3 `:memory:`), schema-synced, through `engine.find` / `engine.aggregate` and the `POST /api/v1/data/:object/query` handler with JSON-round-tripped bodies, `TZ=America/New_York`; 445 (memory) / 452 (SQLite) cells per tree. **PostgreSQL: NOT MEASURED locally** — pg 16 binaries exist, `initdb` ran, but the container refuses the `postgres` service account access to the scratch tree, so no private server could open its data dir; the PG reading of record is CI's `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` job at head (`success`; it runs `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql test` under `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1`, PG at `Asia/Shanghai`, `TZ=America/New_York`, so the new driver-sql file's PG cell — 11 operators × number / `Date` twin / `datetime` control, "an empty table answers no row, not a refusal", create/update — ran and passed there). **MySQL: NOT MEASURED locally**; same CI job. Whole suites, typecheck and the derived gate family were not re-run locally (CI's).

### ① Derived judgments

- **1 · The rows (memory / SQLite, base → head, both doors agree in every cell; `Date` twin at head; `datetime` control base = head):** `$gt` 0→1 / 6→1 · twin 1 · ctrl 3; `$lt` 0→3 / 0→3 · 3 · 2; `$eq` 0→2 / 0→2 · 2 · 1; `$gte` 0→3 / 6→3 · 3 · 4; `$lte` 0→5 / 0→5 · 5 · 3; `$ne` 6→4 / 6→4 · 4 · 5; `$in` 0→3 / 0→3 · 3 · 1; `$nin` 6→3 / 6→3 · 3 · 5; `$between` 0→5 / 0→5 · 5 · 1; implicit 0→2 / 0→2 · 2 · 1; `$eq` UTC-midnight 0→2 / 0→2 · 2 · 0. Head ids identical across the two drivers, engine = REST, number = `Date`, on all 11 operators (`$gt` → `o3`; `$eq` → `o4,o6`; …). Empty object: 0 → 0 on every operator, both drivers. Every `datetime` control cell byte-identical base → head. The dev's table is reproduced cell for cell on memory and SQLite; the PG column (500 → count) is CI-measured at the driver door and otherwise the dev's reading. Bar met on the two drivers I could run; the third by CI.
- **1 · per-aggregation `filter` = `where`:** at head 88/88 keys equal per driver (populated/empty × `date`/`datetime` × 11 operators × engine/REST). At base the `date` `filter` answered 0 on every operator except `$ne` / `$nin` / `$between` = 6, as the PR states. **`having`:** `max(date)` `$gt` N: no group → `c2`; `$eq` N: no group → `c3`; `$in`: no group → `c1,c3`; `$lt` N: no group → `c1`; `min(datetime)` `$gte` N control `c2,c3` unchanged; engine = REST throughout, both drivers.
- **2 · One rule, no collateral:** the only source change is `canonicalCalendarDay` in `temporal-storage-form.ts` (the `date` arm; its docstring updated). No driver source in the diff; no third copy — at head `SqlDriver.toDateOnly` returns `temporalStorageForm(value, 'date')`, `coerceFilterValue` → `toDateOnly`, `temporalFilterValue` → `coerceFilterValue`; `driver-memory` `coerceTemporalValue` → `temporalStorageForm`; objectql `having-filter.ts` reads the same export. Rule sweep 46 shapes × 3 kinds = 138 cells: 124 byte-identical, 14 moved, all `date` × a finite number inside the `Date` range (N, UTC midnight, last ms of day, 0, −0, −1, −86400000, a fraction, a negative fraction, ±8.64e15, year 10000, year 0, year 999). Byte-identical: every `datetime` and `time` cell, and on `date` every `Date`, Invalid Date, `NaN`, ±Infinity, ±8.64e15±1, `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, bigint, boxed `Number`, epoch-ms string, bare day, zone-naive, ISO, offset, wall clocks, `'25:00'`, junk, empty, spaces, `null`, `undefined`, booleans, object, arrays. String comparands on `date` and `datetime` through both doors: 45 cells per driver, 0 moved. All moved end-to-end cells: memory 75/445, SQLite 79/452 — **0 outside "a number on a `date` field"**.
- **3 · Write and read paths (base → head):** `engine.insert` and REST create of a number on a `date` field: `VALIDATION_FAILED` / `HTTP 400 VALIDATION_FAILED` at base and head, both drivers (`datetime` control the same). Direct `driver.create` / `update` of a number on a `date` field: memory and SQLite stored `1769940000000` / `-1` / `1768057200000` → now `"2026-02-01"` / `"1969-12-31"` / `"2026-01-10"`; the same number on `datetime` `"2026-02-01T10:00:00.000Z"` unchanged; PG's `22008` → stored day is CI-measured (write-path test in the PG cell). SQLite raw INTEGER already in a `date` column: `find`, `findOne`, `groupBy` key, `distinct` present `1769940000000` → `"2026-02-01"`; `max` over the mixed group `"2026-01-05"` unchanged; a `where` day comparand against that row `(none)` → `(none)` unchanged. **One cell the changeset does not list:** a `where` with the NUMBER comparand against that raw row matched `x1` at base and matches nothing at head (the comparand becomes day text; the raw INTEGER has no column-side repair on `date`). Judgments: every movement is inside the claim's class (a number on a `date` field, one rule for every caller — the write and read paths call the same function, which is what "the same rule for every caller" means); ADR-0053 Phase 1 step 1 (write normalization: "all collapse to the calendar day") and step 2 (read: "transparently repairs legacy rows") support both movements; the changeset and PR body disclose the write and read movements truthfully; the raw-INTEGER `where`-number cell is undisclosed but reachable only through a raw SQL write (or a base-era direct driver write) — acceptance-note level, not a contract item. **No accept set narrows:** the engine/REST write doors refuse exactly what they refused; the driver doors accept what they accepted (PG's widens from refusal to acceptance); no comparand that answered is refused.
- **4 · Stop valve (ADR-0053 read whole, 1211 lines):** no sentence requires a `date` comparand to be a calendar-day string. The nearest: TL;DR "`date` = a timezone-naive calendar day, represented as a `YYYY-MM-DD` string end-to-end (storage, query, CEL). It is **never** converted to an instant and **never** timezone-shifted." — a rule about the value's representation; the PR converts the comparand to a day, never the date to an instant. Phase 1 decision 1: "A `Date`, a full ISO string, or a `YYYY-MM-DD` string all collapse to the calendar day (UTC calendar day for a `Date`, matching the existing filter coercion)." — non-day inputs collapse, none is refused. D-C1 (sibling kind): "A `Date` / epoch-ms / full-timestamp value folds to its **UTC** time-of-day". The dev's five quotes exist verbatim at head (ADR lines 37–39, 98–100, 633; `filter.zod.ts:349`; `temporal-comparand.ts:60`). Read direction stands; the valve does not trip.
- **5 · The pins discriminate (re-run at head):** anchor line 1 → 0, blob `61a6c0861a` → `2a9bd5d997`, core rebuilt, `dist` marker 0. Mutated: core **13 failed / 59 passed** (dev: 13/59); memory **12 / 11** (dev: 12/11); driver-sql SQLite cell **12 failed / 11 passed / 2 skipped** (PG and MySQL cells unprovisioned here; the dev's 35 failed = these 12 + 23 live-PG cases, 11 passed = SQLite empties — consistent); REST **17 / 1** (dev: 17/1). Restored with `git checkout HEAD -- <path>`: blob `61a6c0861a` = `HEAD:`, `git status --porcelain` 0 lines, `git diff HEAD` empty, core rebuilt (marker 1), pins green again: core 72, memory 23, driver-sql 23 + 2 skipped, REST 18. Direction green → red → green.
- **6 · Clause-② and gates:** no published export or payload key moves (`temporalStorageForm(value, kind): unknown` unchanged; no `api-surface` file in the diff); no request that answered is now refused. `Clause-②: no`, no arm — correct. `check-changeset-no-major --base 805af4f290 --event event.json` (payload built from the live `GET /pulls/20224`, body 16385 bytes, `updated_at 2026-09-27T12:06:33Z`): "✓ This diff introduces no `major` bump." / "✓ LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② `no`, so no package here is declared to have grown a published surface. · declaration line: `Clause-②: no` · direction arm: none declared — the declaration names no widening and no narrowing" — exit 0. `check-adr-0087-registration --base 805af4f290`: "✓ check-adr-0087-registration: this PR adds no declared-breaking changeset (2 non-breaking changeset(s) seen)." — exit 0.
- **7 · Changesets and PR body:** every sentence of `20203-epoch-ms-date-comparand.md` checked against the measurements above is TRUE on memory and SQLite (the base table incl. `filter` `$between` = 6; the head counts 1/3/2/3/5; `$gte`/`$lte`/`$ne`/`$nin`/implicit; `having` groups; the number/`Date` agreement; negative and fractional numbers; the write and read paths; the "not changed" list). Its PG sentences (`22008` at base, the day at head) are corroborated by the card's pointer 5854552106 and CI's PG cell, not measured here. **`20176-*` DELIBERATE CORRECTION — confirmed as written:** old "The copies agreed on every shape measured when they were lifted, so no `where`, write or read answer of either driver changes." → new "The copies agreed on every shape measured when they were lifted, so the lift itself changes no `where`, write or read answer of either driver (#20203, in the same release, then reads an epoch-millisecond number on a `date` field as its UTC calendar day)." The new sentence is TRUE at head (the lift was a move; #20203 moves the number-on-`date` cells and nothing else); 35 lines before and after, only line 31 differs, every other line byte-identical. Other pending notes: `20148-aggregation-filter-keys-rest` carries no temporal-comparand claim — reads true; `20148-aggregation-filter-where-doors`'s forward pointer "(#20176 closes both in the same release, …)" is true and its "Not changed, measured identical before and after" sentence is scoped to its own change — reads true. No other pending changeset states a core / driver-sql / driver-memory temporal behaviour this PR moves. **PR body: no FALSE sentence found**; the live-PG readings and whole-suite counts are the dev's, taken as CI-corroborated. `SqlDriver.toDateOnly`'s docstring "Anything else (and `null`/`undefined`) passes through unchanged" is now FALSE for a finite number; it is driver-sql source prose (a `protected` member's TSDoc), none of the five review faces → an acceptance note, as the seat ruled, not a contract item; the same class as `memory-temporal.ts`'s module note "so every answer this driver gives is unchanged" (about the lift).
- **8 · Year spelling (for the seat's filing; not a verdict item):** rule output at head `"999-06-15"`, `"10000-01-01"`, `"-1-01-01"` (base: the number unchanged). REST on the six rows, memory / SQLite, base → head: year 999 `$gt` 0→0 / 6→0, `$lt` 0→6 / 0→6; year 10000 `$gt` 0→6 / 6→6, `$lt` 0→0 / 0→0; year −1 `$gt` 0→6 / 6→6, `$lt` 0→0 / 0→0. Correct answers are 6/0, 0/6, 6/0. **Head is worse than base on:** SQLite year 999 `$gt` (6→0) and `$lt` (0→6) — base's INTEGER-below-TEXT accident happened to give the right rows; memory year 999 `$lt` (0→6); memory year 10000 `$gt` (0→6). Head is better on memory year −1 `$gt` (0→6). Number = `Date` at head on every year cell, and the `Date` cells are identical base → head — the unpadded spelling is the pre-existing `Date`-arm defect; this PR routes numbers into it and discloses exactly these readings (out-of-scope finding 2). PG (the dev: 999 and 10000 correct, −1 a 500): NOT MEASURED here.
- **9 · Scope and merge:** see Scope — `packages/spec` and every driver `src/` non-test file untouched; probe merge-tree onto `origin/main` clean.
- **10 · CI at head (read last, all 34 check-runs completed):** 30 `success`, 3 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)), 1 `failure`. The seven required contexts are all `success`: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Governed Surface Queue Guard. The one failure is **Check Changeset**, by design, on exactly `.changeset/20176-aggregation-temporal-storage-rule.md`; its log: "✓ No empty-frontmatter changeset introduced by this diff … This PR changes a changeset it did not add: .changeset/20176-aggregation-temporal-storage-rule.md — present on the merge base and CHANGED by this PR" and "##[error].changeset/20176-aggregation-temporal-storage-rule.md exists on the merge base and was not added by this PR, so changing or deleting it silently replaces somebody else's release note (#17712). … DELIBERATE CORRECTION -- your change may have made this PENDING release note false, and you rewrote it in the same stroke. Remedy: do NOT restore it -- say so on the PR and get it confirmed". No other failure.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `20203-*`: `patch` × `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-memory`, `@objectstack/objectql`. Consistent with `Clause-②: no`: a fix that moves answers on an already-accepted input and changes no public surface stays `patch` under the launch-window rule; `objectql` is graded although its source did not move because its `filter` / `having` answers move through core — acceptable. `20176-*` keeps its levels (minor/minor/patch/patch) unchanged. Level axis and ADR-0087 gate both exit 0 (quoted above).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions[0]` (unpadded year spelling) → the seat ruled **A**; I concur on the measurements: number ≡ `Date` across the whole `Date` range at head, the `Date` cells are byte-identical base → head, and a pad would move `Date` cells. Filed separately; my year cells above are for that card.
- Out-of-scope finding 1 (`driver-mongodb`'s own `storageDateValue` copy): not measurable here (no server); source not re-read; carrier none, as ruled.
- Out-of-scope finding 3 (`toDateOnly` docstring now false for a number): acceptance note, carrier none, as ruled; recommend a one-line docstring correction ride on the next driver-sql source PR (it is prose that now advertises behaviour the code does not have).
- Reviewer flag (new, acceptance-note level): `where` with a NUMBER comparand against a raw INTEGER already in a SQLite `date` column matched at base and does not at head; raw-write-only reach; inside the class; not disclosed in the changeset.
- Reviewer observation (no action): `20176-*` line 35 ("Not changed, measured identical before and after on both drivers: every `where` answer…") uses the same per-change before/after idiom as line 31 did; it states that PR's own measurement and the corrected line 31 now disambiguates the release — not FALSE.
- PostgreSQL and MySQL cells are CI-measured, not locally measured, for the reason in Scope.
